slides.0.title: Course Introduction
slides.0.content:
If Anjou Blanc is the entry course for Chenin dry whites and Saumur Blanc is the intermediate class, then Savennières is the doctoral thesis. This tiny 145-hectare AOC and its two independent Crus — Coulée de Serrant and La Roche-aux-Moines — have been called "one of the world's greatest dry white wines" by British wine writer Hugh Johnson.

Course Learning Objectives

🌋 Volcanic Terroir

Understand the unique combination of volcanic rock + schist + sand in Savennières, and its impact on Chenin Blanc

🏆 The Trilogy: Savennières → La Roche-aux-Moines → Coulée de Serrant

Master the history, area, regulations, and progressive styles of the three tiers

🌱 Nicolas Joly and Biodynamic Viticulture

Understand Coulée de Serrant's history as the spiritual origin of the global biodynamic wine movement

🍷 Aging Potential and Tasting Techniques

From youthful austerity to beeswax oxidation — master the 30-year flavor evolution of Savennières
slides.1.title: Savennières — The Golden Slopes of Western Loire
slides.1.highlights.0.title: South-Facing Slope
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Located on south-facing slopes on the Loire's north bank, excellent sun exposure, 1–2°C warmer than surroundings
slides.1.highlights.1.title: High Slope Ventilation
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Slope gradient 15–30°, natural ventilation reduces disease risk, suitable for hand cultivation
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Three-Color Soils
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Volcanic rock (Spilite/Phtanite) + Schist + Sandy alluvium (Sand) combined
slides.1.content:
Savennières is situated in a unique topographic position on the north bank of the Loire River in western Anjou — the river bends sharply here, and sunlight strikes the steep slope directly from the south, creating a rare "south-facing high slope" (coteaux exposés sud) zone in the Loire Valley. This hillside not only enjoys excellent sun exposure, but its soil composition is among the most complex in Loire.

🌋 Spilite & Phtanite (Volcanic Rock)

From Precambrian and Cambrian submarine volcanic activity. Spilite is a light green metamorphic basalt; Phtanite is an extremely hard black siliceous rock. Both heat up quickly and retain warmth, imparting tropical mineral and graphite notes to the grapes.

🪨 Brioverian Schist

The same Precambrian schist as the main body of Anjou — blue-gray to black, imparting flint and smoky character to Chenin.

🏖️ Sandy Alluvium

Sandy soils formed from Loire river deposits, concentrated at the slope's base, drains extremely rapidly, giving wines softness.

⏳ Aging Potential Spectrum

  • 0–3 years: Austere, green apple, quince, lemon zest, flint, phenolic grip (grapefruit pith)
  • 3–10 years: Beeswax, chamomile, toasted hazelnuts, emerging mineral depth, gradually rounder palate
  • 10–20 years: Madeira-like oxidative notes, curry, dry hay, candied orange peel, foie gras-like richness
  • 20–30+ years: Top wines retain their core acidity and complete structure (Coulée de Serrant 1980s vintages still vibrant)
slides.1.quiz.question: What is the geographical distinction of Savennières in the Loire Valley?
slides.1.quiz.options.0: Located at the source of the Loire River
slides.1.quiz.options.1: South-facing steep slopes on the Loire's north bank, with excellent sun exposure and ventilation
slides.1.quiz.explanation: Most of the Loire Valley consists of gentle alluvial plains, while Savennières sits on the north bank where the Loire makes a large bend near Angers — creating rare "south-facing steep slopes" (gradient 15–30°) with excellent sunshine, natural drainage, and good ventilation. This unique topography is key to why Savennières can produce top Chenin dry whites with exceptional aging potential in the relatively cool Loire climate.
slides.3.title: The Savennières Trilogy
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Coulée de Serrant
slides.3.highlights.1.title: La Roche-aux-Moines
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Savennières
slides.3.highlights.2.content: 105 ha main AOC, the broader appellation
slides.3.content:
The Savennières hierarchy expands outward in three tiers: at the apex is an extremely small single-vineyard AOC, in the middle is a Cru AOC shared by multiple estates, and at the base is the regional AOC. Each tier has its own history, production regulations, and style.

🥇 Coulée de Serrant (Single Vineyard AOC)

  • Area: 7 ha
  • Ownership: Exclusively owned by the Joly family since their 1962 purchase (Domaine de la Coulée de Serrant)
  • History: Planted by Cistercian monks in 1130; praised by King Louis XI and novelist Honoré de Balzac
  • Viticulture: Fully biodynamic since the 1980s
  • Regulations: Yield limit 25 hL/ha (strictest dry white in Loire); 100% Chenin Blanc Sec
  • Style: Beeswax, curry, dried herbs, extraordinary length; 30+ year aging potential
  • Price: €120–200/bottle (young vintages); aged vintages €300+

🥈 La Roche-aux-Moines (Cru AOC)

  • Area: 33 ha
  • Ownership: Shared by several estates (largest: Domaine aux Moines, ~9 ha)
  • History: Planted by monks of Saint-Nicolas in 1106; named after the monastery
  • Regulations: Yield limit 30 hL/ha; 100% Chenin Blanc Sec
  • Style: More direct than Coulée, firm structure, strong mineral tension
  • Key producers: Domaine aux Moines, Château de Chamboureau, Domaine du Closel

🥉 Savennières (Main AOC)

  • Area: ~105 ha (excluding the two Crus)
  • Regulations: Yield limit 50 hL/ha; 100% Chenin Blanc Sec
  • Key producers: Domaine du Closel, Domaine des Baumard, Domaine du Petit Métris, Château d'Epiré
  • Style: Ranges from clean and crisp to firm-structured, depending on the estate's approach
slides.4.title: Nicolas Joly and the Story of Biodynamic Viticulture
slides.4.highlights.0.title: 1980s Conversion
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Returned from the finance industry to the family estate; fully adopted biodynamic farming from 1984
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Wine from Sky to Earth
slides.4.highlights.1.content: The 1997 book became the bible of the global natural wine movement
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Renaissance des Appellations
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Founded the international biodynamic wine organization; members span 16 countries and 200+ estates
slides.4.content:
Nicolas Joly's story is a turning point in the late 20th-century wine world. After returning from a career at J.P. Morgan in New York to the family estate, he read Rudolf Steiner's anthroposophical agricultural writings in 1984 and made the bold decision to convert Coulée de Serrant entirely to biodynamic farming. At the time, this was considered madness — but 30 years later, the world's top estates (DRC, Leflaive, Chapoutier, etc.) had followed suit, proving Joly's foresight.

🌙 Core Principles of Biodynamic Farming

  • Preparation 500/501: Cow manure stuffed into cow horns and buried in soil to ferment — a microbial activator
  • Lunar calendar: Using Maria Thun's lunar calendar to determine timing for cultivation, pruning, and bottling
  • No synthetic chemicals: Banning artificial fertilizers, herbicides, pesticides, and cultivated yeasts
  • Holistic farming: Vineyard integrated with cattle, horses, chickens, bees, and cover crops

🌍 Renaissance des Appellations International Organization

The international biodynamic wine organization Joly founded in the 1990s; current members include:

  • France: Domaine Leflaive, Comte Lafon, Marcel Deiss, Zind-Humbrecht
  • Germany: Dr. Bürklin-Wolf, Wittmann
  • Italy: Foradori, Stella di Campalto
  • Austria: Nikolaihof, Bernhard Ott
  • 200+ estates in 16 countries with regular touring exhibitions
slides.4.quiz.question: When Nicolas Joly converted Coulée de Serrant to biodynamic farming in 1984, whose writings inspired him?
slides.4.quiz.explanation: Nicolas Joly was inspired by Rudolf Steiner (1861–1925) and his 1924 "Agriculture Course." Steiner was an Austrian philosopher and founder of Anthroposophy, who proposed treating the farm as an organic whole and introduced concepts of lunar cycles, stellar movements, and special preparations. Steiner's theories form the basis of global biodynamic agriculture (Demeter certification system), long considered "mysticism" by mainstream agronomy. Joly is among the few who fully applied them to top-level winemaking.
slides.5.title: Level 3-2 Knowledge Test
slides.5.questions.0.question: What are the area and ownership of Coulée de Serrant?
slides.5.questions.0.options.1: 7 ha, exclusively owned by the Joly family
slides.5.questions.0.explanation: Coulée de Serrant is an extremely rare example in Loire — a "single vineyard + single owner AOC" (similar to Burgundy's Romanée-Conti). Just 7 ha, exclusively operated by the Joly family since their 1962 purchase. This structure gives the estate complete control over style and quality, making it a very special existence within the French AOC system.
slides.5.questions.1.question: The volcanic rocks in Savennières AOC are mainly composed of which two rock types?
slides.5.questions.1.explanation: Spilite is a light green metamorphic basalt (Precambrian), while Phtanite is an extremely hard black siliceous rock. These two rock types formed from Precambrian to Cambrian submarine volcanic activity, and are a key component of Savennières' terroir. They heat up quickly and retain warmth, imparting tropical mineral and graphite notes to the grapes — the biggest difference from the main body of Anjou Blanc (pure schist).
slides.5.questions.2.question: What is the pyramid hierarchy of the Savennières system from innermost to outermost?
slides.5.questions.2.options.0: Savennières → La Roche-aux-Moines → Coulée de Serrant
slides.5.questions.2.options.1: Coulée de Serrant → La Roche-aux-Moines → Savennières
slides.5.questions.2.options.2: La Roche-aux-Moines → Coulée de Serrant → Savennières
slides.5.questions.2.options.3: Savennières → Coulée de Serrant → La Roche-aux-Moines
slides.5.questions.2.explanation: From the most prestigious (smallest, strictest) to the broadest: Coulée de Serrant (7 ha, single-vineyard AOC, yield 25 hL/ha) → La Roche-aux-Moines (33 ha, Cru AOC, 30 hL/ha) → Savennières (105 ha main AOC, 50 hL/ha). This structure is analogous to Burgundy's Grand Cru → Premier Cru → Village logic.
slides.5.questions.3.question: After 20 years of aging, what aroma profile most commonly appears in top Savennières?
slides.5.questions.3.options.1: Beeswax, curry, Madeira-like oxidative notes, dry hay
slides.5.questions.3.explanation: The hallmark aromatic evolution of aged top Chenin Blanc dry wines: youthful green apple, quince, and lemon zest gradually develop into beeswax, toasted hazelnuts, curry (fenugreek/Sotolon), Madeira-like oxidative notes, dry hay, and candied orange peel. This aromatic profile — unique to Chenin — is fundamentally different from Riesling or top old Chardonnay, and is the key fingerprint for identifying aged Savennières or Vouvray Sec.
